content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts for tenant MarinerInsurance on dedicated-us-west-2-03. Error rate spiked from ~0.2% to 12% in the last 3m. Paging oncall-ryan.
oncall-ryan: acked. I'm on it — pulling up dashboards now. Slack-threading this channel for coordination.
eng-sre-jamie: grabbing logs and the cluster-level health. Do we have a correlation with KV evictions or QPS per-tenant? cc @eng-runtime-sarah
eng-runtime-sarah: early signs: sustained GPU utilization at 96% on pool gpu-p3-03 and high inflight queue length. KV miss rate for Mariner is through the roof -> frequent cache reloads. Looks like large batched sequences from one tenant.
eng-ml-diego: Mariner recently rolled a prompt-scoring job with long-context evals? They mentioned a nightly benchmark yesterday in account notes.
prod-manager-ana: customer impact: Mariner reported 15% of their requests failing, affecting a real-time underwriting flow. They're flagged P1.
oncall-ryan: PagerDuty log: escalation to oncall at 4512346790. Starting mitigation checklist: 1) identify noisy tenant/worker 2) rate-limit or move noisy traffic 3) enable emergency fallback routing 4) coordinate with customer.
eng-sre-jamie: Running tenant QPS query: `sum by(tenant)(rate(requests_total[1m]))` -> MarinerInsurance shows 7.8k rps on model/gpt-3.2-large while expected steady-state ~800 rps. That's the noisy neighbor.
eng-runtime-sarah: Candidate short-term mitigations: - soft throttle Mariner to 1200 rps - route excess to secondary fallback model (compatible but higher latency) - spin standby workers in same region (if capacity) - set eviction threshold to be more aggressive for KV cache items belonging to that tenant.
oncall-ryan: Trying soft throttle first. Applying token bucket rate limit via routing rule now.
eng-runtime-sarah: `kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: rconf/v1
kind: RoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: throttle-mariner-temp
spec:
  match: tenant=="MarinerInsurance"
  rateLimit: {requestsPerSec: 20}
EOF`
eng-sre-jamie: Throttle applied. Observing immediate drop in inflight queue for the pool. 5xx rate down from 12% -> 6% in the next 30s.
customer-ops-mike: Mariner ops on the line: they confirm some requests succeeded but latency increased. They asked what caused this and whether we can avoid throttling their critical flows.
prod-manager-ana: Noted. We're in emergency mitigation — informing customer and planning a safer handoff. Diego can you check whether their benchmark job is coming from service account `mariner-batch-evals`?
eng-ml-diego: Yes, logs show a flurry from `mariner-batch-evals@mariner`. It launched a concurrent sweep across 40 threads with long sequences. Looks like a misconfigured cron.
eng-runtime-sarah: We can 1) isolate that service account via route deny-list for now 2) schedule a quick customer rollback/stop of the cron 3) propose rate-limits for background jobs.
oncall-ryan: Reached out to customer-ops-mike: please ask them to pause `mariner-batch-evals` immediately. I'll prepare an on-platform isolation if they can't.
customer-ops-mike: Sent message to their infra team to pause. ETA ~2m.
incident-bot: System note: cluster autoscale attempted to add 2 nodes at 4512346810 but failed due to quota limits in the customer's reserved pool.
eng-sre-jamie: Quota hit — dedicated pool has a hard cap (reserved). We can't autoscale more GPUs. Options: 1) preemptively evict less-critical tenants on the same pool if policy allows 2) re-route Mariner overflow to a shared fallback pool in another region (cross-region latency impact) 3) negotiate emergency capacity with infra.
eng-runtime-sarah: Evicting other tenants will cause customer impact downstream. Prefer to isolate Mariner and shift their overflow to fallback-us-west-2-burst which has mixed capacity.
oncall-ryan: Can we create a temporary route rule to send excess requests (beyond 1200 rps) to fallback-us-west-2-burst? That keeps other dedicated tenants stable.
eng-runtime-sarah: Implementing now:

apiVersion: rconf/v1
kind: RoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: mariner-overflow-to-fallback
spec:
  match: tenant=="MarinerInsurance" && requestsPerSec > 20
  action: route_to(fallback-us-west-2-burst)

eng-sre-jamie: Rule live. Observability: traffic split ~85% to dedicated, ~15% to fallback. 5xx continuing to trend down to ~2.1%. Gateway timeouts dropping.
customer-ops-mike: Mariner confirms they paused the cron — the flood stopped on their side. Great, thanks. They want a postmortem on why the cron ran uncontrolled.
prod-manager-ana: We'll schedule a follow-up with CS and the customer success manager. For now, we need a runbook update: auto-throttle heuristics for tenant spikes, and alert thresholds earlier.
eng-ml-diego: Suggestion: add a scoring layer that tags heavy batch jobs and forces them to use a batch queue rather than production dedicated lanes.
eng-runtime-sarah: Agreed. I'll open a ticket for runtime changes: backpressure policy, tenant-level burst budgets, and a safer default for KV eviction thresholds.
oncall-ryan: Quick verification: running synthetic p95 latency probes for Mariner -> stable at ~420ms to fallback vs 180ms on dedicated. Error rate at 0.3% now. Marking incident as mitigated in the channel but remaining in watch for 30m.
eng-sre-jamie: Noting what we did for postmortem: root cause = runaway batch eval from `mariner-batch-evals` causing sustained high token generation and KV thrash; contributed by reserved pool quota preventing autoscale; mitigations = soft throttle, overflow routing to fallback, customer pause of job.
prod-manager-ana: I'll draft customer-facing incident summary. Include recommended actions: enforce service-account quotas, add pre-deploy checks for long-context jobs, and opt-in burst capacity tiers.
customer-ops-mike: Mariner appreciates the quick response. They accepted a temporary request cap and asked for a follow-up plan. Also requested any logs we can share for their internal RCA.
eng-runtime-sarah: I'll export the relevant request traces and KV eviction logs and share to the secure S3 bucket for customer with redaction.
incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigated -> monitoring. Node-level metrics normalized; SLO error budget impact estimate: +0.05% for the hour for this customer region.
oncall-ryan: Confirming watch: I'll stay on cleanup and ensure route rules are reverted after 60m if stable. If anything spikes again, we'll escalate to infra for emergency capacity procurement.
eng-sre-jamie: Adding post-incident tasks to the incident board: - runbook update - add tenant spike autoscale fallback - alert tuning - customer follow-up docs
eng-ml-diego: I'll reach out to their ML engineer to recommend better batching settings for their eval job.
oncall-ryan: Thanks everyone. Dropping a short blameless note here for the postmortem. Closing active paging but keeping thread open until last_message_ts.
customer-ops-mike: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
eng-runtime-sarah: Leaving final note: consider adding a preemptive tenant burst cap enforcement soon. I'll file PR for policy changes.
eng-sre-jamie: 30m watch started at 4512346820. If stable, we'll close the incident at 4512347100.
